author: opt-W4

contract.sync_assumed: warp convergence of the 32 lanes, the caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage or the output buffer by a __syncwarp (the harness does)
contract.sync_performed: 7 __syncwarp per call (one more merge level, whose split is trivial), no shuffles, no barriers
contract.k_range: powers of two in [32, N/2] (every merge level must split evenly over the 32 lanes), measured 64, 256 and 1024
contract.n_range: N = 32 x IPT with IPT a power of two in [4, 64], measured 1024 and 2048
contract.type_constraints: fp32 as a 64-bit word in registers (twiddled key high, inverted index low) stored as a key half and an index half in two 32-bit shared arrays, bf16 as one 32-bit word (16 twiddled key bits above the inverted 16-bit index, N at most 65536), int32 indices from the blocked position. Temp storage 54656 bytes for fp32 N 2048 k 1024 (64 runs of 32 at level 0), 31520 for bf16
contract.nan_behavior: twiddled bitwise: a positive NaN orders above +inf, a negative NaN below -inf, the all-ones negative NaN collides with the all-zero absent-item filler word (never produced by focus-set inputs). -0.0 is folded onto +0.0 before the twiddle (one FADD for fp32, one compare and select for bf16), so both zeros form one tie class ordered by index
contract.tie_break_support: inherent: the word order is (key descending, index ascending), the merge path takes the first run on ties and the chunk network compares full words, prefer_smaller_index is the same binary as not_guaranteed
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent at zero extra cost: slot r holds rank r

low_level: Same session and lock section as the control W4_wmerge (v4): 80 to 165 registers, no spill, no stack, 3808 to 14392 SASS instructions for two calls (the control 3672 to 16104), temp storage 15648 to 54656 bytes (the control 12384 to 48128).
algorithmic: Against W4_wmerge in one section (latency, both requirements identical): bf16 N 1024 k 64 5910 against 5413, k 256 9020 against 8408, N 2048 k 64 9945 against 9036, k 256 14531 against 13540, k 1024 20779 against 19780; fp32 N 1024 k 64 12164 against 11342, k 256 17984 against 17191, N 2048 k 64 19535 against 19146, k 256 30113 against 29580, k 1024 43326 against 42596. 0.91x to 0.98x everywhere: two sorts of 32 (382 exchanges) plus a merge level of 64 outputs per lane cost more than one sort of 64 (543 exchanges).
negative: The idea that the 64-word fp32 sort is slow because of the 128 live registers does not survive this test: halving the live words did not recover the sort's cost at any cell, so the per-exchange cost of the 64-bit word (two ISETP, four SEL) and the one-warp issue rate are what the sort pays.
surprises: In the v3 build (xor layout, exact counts) the same variant had won 1.31x at fp32 N 2048 k 256 and 1.06x at k 1024, a register-pressure effect of that build (255 registers), gone in v4 at 128 to 168 registers.
open_questions: Whether four pieces of 16 with two lane-local merge levels behave differently is untested, the trend here says no.

correctness_notes: All 20 cells passed the oracle battery under both requirements, one latency-only batch (label v4_halves) on umbriel-b200-091, source commit 0ba868b00d.
